project.name: LLMFA Financial Analysis Dashboard
project.purpose: Analyse a company's historical financial performance, latest-year changes, financial strength, valuation, and transparent future scenarios using traceable data.
project.latest_year_comparison: Latest available completed financial year versus the immediately preceding comparable financial year
design_principles: Keep seven primary chart modules; do not add charts merely to increase chart count.
Use source-traceable figures and clearly distinguish reported values from derived metrics.
Never silently mix consolidated and standalone data.
Represent missing values as null, never as zero.
Show actuals, company guidance, sourced analyst estimates, and model scenarios distinctly.
Use sector-specific metrics for banks, NBFCs, insurers, and other businesses where general industrial-company ratios are unsuitable.
Every chart should answer a clear financial question and provide concise, evidence-based observations.

core_raw_variables.name: ebit
core_raw_variables.label: EBIT / Operating Profit
core_raw_variables.definition_note: Use one documented EBIT definition consistently; do not silently substitute another reported subtotal.

core_raw_variables.name: ebitda
core_raw_variables.label: EBITDA
core_raw_variables.definition_note: Prefer reported EBITDA when clearly defined; otherwise derive only using a documented formula.

core_raw_variables.name: capex
core_raw_variables.label: Capital Expenditure
core_raw_variables.sign_convention: Store/display capex as a positive spending amount for FCF calculation; preserve original reported sign in source record.

core_raw_variables.name: interest_bearing_debt
core_raw_variables.label: Interest-Bearing Debt
core_raw_variables.definition_note: Document which short-term and long-term borrowings/lease liabilities are included.

source_priority: Company annual report and audited financial statements
Reputable financial-data providers, with source and date recorded
validation_rules: Validate company identity, financial year, period-end date, reporting basis, currency, and units before plotting.
Do not silently mix consolidated and standalone data.
Missing values remain null; do not impute zero.
Flag restatements, reclassifications, changes in accounting definitions, and unusual fiscal-year lengths.
Store source-reported values separately from normalized and derived values.
Check ratios and growth rates for zero, negative, or otherwise unsuitable denominators.
Record market-data as-of date separately from financial-statement period.
Show warnings where data is incomplete or definitions are not comparable.

chart_sections.title: Revenue & Profit Growth
chart_sections.purpose: Show the scale and direction of the company's business and earnings over time.
chart_sections.time_horizon: Previous five financial years, or the longest comparable period available up to five years
chart_types: multi-series line chart with metric selector

derived_metrics.name: revenue_growth_yoy
derived_metrics.caveat: Do not present as an ordinary growth rate when the prior value is zero or the sign change makes comparison misleading.

derived_metrics.name: ebit_growth_yoy
derived_metrics.caveat: Apply denominator and sign-change checks.

derived_metrics.name: ebitda_growth_yoy
derived_metrics.caveat: Apply denominator and sign-change checks.

derived_metrics.name: pat_growth_yoy
derived_metrics.caveat: Flag transitions between profit and loss; do not imply a conventional growth rate where it is not meaningful.

derived_metrics.name: five_year_cagr
derived_metrics.caveat: Five annual observations normally represent four intervals; calculate only when endpoints are positive and comparable.

key_questions: Is revenue growing consistently?
Are EBIT, EBITDA, and PAT growing faster or slower than revenue?
Is growth stable, accelerating, slowing, or volatile?
visual_rules: Do not put revenue, EBIT, EBITDA, and PAT on one unlabelled axis if their scales obscure smaller series.
Offer metric selection or indexed trends with a clearly stated base year of 100.
Show units, financial years, reporting basis, and missing periods.
automated_insights: Five-year trend or CAGR where meaningful
data_warnings: Flag exceptional items or restatements where identified.
Keep definitions of EBIT and EBITDA consistent across years.

chart_sections.title: Profitability & Capital Efficiency
chart_sections.purpose: Evaluate margins and how effectively the company uses shareholder and operating capital.
chart_types: separate line chart or metric selector for return ratios

derived_metrics.name: roe
derived_metrics.caveat: Average equity normally uses opening and closing equity; document treatment when either is unavailable or negative.

derived_metrics.name: roce
derived_metrics.caveat: Use one documented capital-employed definition consistently.

key_questions: Are margins expanding or contracting?
Is the company earning stronger returns on capital?
Is growth accompanied by improving capital efficiency?
visual_rules: Use percentage axes and distinguish margin ratios from return ratios.
Do not compare ratios across companies without checking accounting definitions and sector comparability.
automated_insights: Growth accompanied by improving or declining profitability
data_warnings: Ratios may be misleading with negative revenue, equity, or capital employed.
Banks and financial companies require sector-specific interpretation.

chart_sections.title: Cash Flow & Earnings Quality
chart_sections.purpose: Assess whether reported earnings convert into cash and how much cash remains after capital expenditure.
chart_types: grouped bar chart for PAT and operating cash flow
bar chart for CapEx and free cash flow

derived_metrics.name: free_cash_flow
derived_metrics.caveat: CapEx must be normalized as a positive spending amount for this formula.

derived_metrics.name: cash_conversion
derived_metrics.caveat: Show as unavailable or specially labelled when PAT is zero or negative.

key_questions: Does operating cash flow broadly support reported PAT?
Is free cash flow positive and sustainable?
Is capital expenditure increasing, and is it being funded by operations or external capital?
visual_rules: Use a zero baseline where appropriate to show negative cash flow clearly.
Do not treat one year's negative FCF as automatically bad; explain the trend and investment context.
automated_insights: CapEx burden and cash conversion trend
data_warnings: Cash flow can be volatile because of working capital and timing.
Separate recurring operating patterns from one-off transactions when data permits.

chart_sections.title: Debt & Financial Safety
chart_sections.purpose: Evaluate leverage, liquidity buffers, and the company's ability to service and repay debt.
chart_sections.time_horizon: Previous five financial years, highlighting latest position

derived_metrics.name: net_debt
derived_metrics.formula: Interest-Bearing Debt - Cash and Cash Equivalents

derived_metrics.name: debt_to_equity
derived_metrics.caveat: Not meaningful in the usual way when equity is zero or negative.

derived_metrics.name: interest_coverage
derived_metrics.caveat: A simplified measure; document the definitions and handle zero finance costs.

derived_metrics.name: net_debt_to_ebitda
derived_metrics.caveat: Use cautiously or mark not meaningful when EBITDA is zero or negative.

key_questions: Is debt rising faster than earnings?
Does the company have enough cash and operating earnings to service debt?
Is the balance sheet becoming safer or more fragile?
visual_rules: Show debt and cash as separate series and net debt as a derived metric.
Distinguish gross debt from net debt.
Include the definition of debt used, including whether lease liabilities are included.
automated_insights: Leverage rising or falling relative to EBITDA
data_warnings: Negative net debt means net cash under the selected definition.
Financial-sector leverage should not be interpreted using industrial-company thresholds.

chart_sections.title: Working Capital & Liquidity
chart_sections.purpose: Identify short-term liquidity pressure and changes in cash tied up in receivables and inventory.
chart_sections.time_horizon: Previous five financial years, highlighting latest position
chart_types: current assets versus current liabilities chart

derived_metrics.name: current_ratio
derived_metrics.caveat: Not meaningful when current liabilities are zero; interpretation varies by sector.

derived_metrics.name: receivables_days
derived_metrics.caveat: If credit sales are unavailable, label the revenue-based estimate as a proxy.

derived_metrics.name: inventory_days
derived_metrics.caveat: Requires a comparable COGS definition and appropriate average inventory data.

key_questions: Are receivables taking longer to collect?
Is inventory accumulating faster than sales or cost of goods sold?
Is short-term liquidity improving or deteriorating?
visual_rules: Use average opening/closing balances for days-based metrics when available.
Label proxy calculations and show unavailable metrics rather than silently substituting values.
data_warnings: This module needs sector-specific interpretation for many financial businesses.

chart_sections.title: Latest FY vs Previous FY Financial Comparison
chart_sections.purpose: Provide a direct, auditable comparison between the latest available completed financial year and the prior comparable year.

derived_metrics.name: absolute_change
derived_metrics.formula: Latest FY Value - Previous FY Value

derived_metrics.name: yoy_percentage_change
derived_metrics.formula: ((Latest FY Value - Previous FY Value) / abs(Previous FY Value)) * 100
derived_metrics.caveat: Handle zero, negative, and sign-changing prior values explicitly; display not meaningful when needed.

key_questions: What improved or deteriorated in the latest year?
Which key values changed the most in absolute and percentage terms?
Do profit and cash-flow changes tell the same story?
visual_rules: Do not place all eight metrics on one raw-value axis because scales differ.
Use a metric selector or separate appropriately scaled views.
Display financial year labels, units, reporting basis, and source references.
automated_insights: Conflicting revenue, profit, and cash-flow trends
data_warnings: Compare like-for-like periods and the same reporting basis.
Flag changes caused by restatements or reclassification.

chart_sections.title: Valuation & Future Outlook
chart_sections.purpose: Compare current valuation with relevant peers and explore transparent possible financial outcomes.

time_horizon.market_snapshot: Latest available market data with a visible as-of date
time_horizon.historical_context: Historical valuation multiples where reliable data is available
time_horizon.scenarios: Next one to three financial years

chart_types: historical valuation trend when reliable data exists

derived_metrics.name: market_capitalisation
derived_metrics.caveat: Use an appropriate share count and corporate-action-adjusted price where relevant.

derived_metrics.name: enterprise_value
derived_metrics.formula: Market Capitalisation + Debt-Like Obligations - Cash and Cash Equivalents
derived_metrics.caveat: Document included debt-like obligations and use a consistent EV definition.

derived_metrics.name: ev_to_ebitda
derived_metrics.caveat: Usually not meaningful when EBITDA is zero or negative.

derived_metrics.name: pe_ratio
derived_metrics.formula: Market Capitalisation / Profit Attributable to Equity Shareholders
derived_metrics.caveat: Usually not meaningful when attributable earnings are zero or negative.

derived_metrics.name: price_to_book
derived_metrics.caveat: Interpret carefully when equity is zero or negative.

scenario_formulas.name: forecast_revenue
scenario_formulas.formula: Previous Year Revenue * (1 + Assumed Revenue Growth Rate)

scenario_formulas.name: forecast_pat
scenario_formulas.caveat: A simplified approach; assumptions should reflect financing costs, taxes, and exceptional items where possible.

scenario_formulas.name: forecast_free_cash_flow
scenario_formulas.formula: Forecast Operating Cash Flow - Forecast CapEx

scenario_requirements: Create bear, base, and bull cases with explicit assumptions.
Record the source and rationale for company guidance or any external estimates.
Label model-generated values as scenarios, not predictions or reported facts.
Show sensitivity to revenue growth, margins, CapEx, and cash conversion where data supports it.
Compare peers only when business models, fiscal periods, and accounting definitions are reasonably comparable.
key_questions: How does valuation compare with relevant peers and the company's own history?
What expectations may already be reflected in the current valuation?
What assumptions drive the bear, base, and bull scenarios?
How sensitive are projected earnings and cash flows to changes in assumptions?
visual_rules: Label market-data dates and valuation definitions.
Separate actuals, company guidance, sourced analyst estimates, and model scenarios visually and in the data schema.
automated_insights: Relative peer valuation with comparability caveats
Valuation sensitivity to growth and margin assumptions
data_warnings: Peer multiples can be misleading across sectors or accounting definitions.
Scenario outputs are not guaranteed predictions.
Do not use stale market prices without displaying their as-of date.

additional_compact_section.title: Shareholder Returns & Capital Allocation
additional_compact_section.presentation: Compact table or small supporting visual; not a new primary chart module by default
additional_compact_section.purpose: Show whether company growth translates into per-share progress and how cash is allocated.

optional_metrics.name: eps_growth
optional_metrics.label: Earnings Per Share Growth
optional_metrics.formula: Calculate year-on-year change in EPS with zero/negative denominator safeguards.

optional_metrics.name: shares_outstanding_change
optional_metrics.label: Change in Shares Outstanding
optional_metrics.formula: Latest shares outstanding - previous period shares outstanding

optional_metrics.name: dividend_payout_ratio
optional_metrics.label: Dividend Payout Ratio
optional_metrics.formula: Dividends attributable to ordinary shareholders / PAT attributable to ordinary shareholders
optional_metrics.caveat: Only when earnings and dividend definitions are comparable and the denominator is meaningful.

optional_metrics.name: dividend_per_share
optional_metrics.label: Dividend Per Share
optional_metrics.formula: Use reported dividend per share and record the relevant financial year.

optional_metrics.name: buybacks
optional_metrics.label: Share Buybacks
optional_metrics.formula: Use reported buyback data where available.

optional_metrics.name: capex_and_acquisitions
optional_metrics.label: CapEx and Acquisitions
optional_metrics.formula: Show reported amounts separately where available.

key_questions: Is EPS growing in line with total profit?
Has share issuance diluted existing shareholders?
How much capital is returned to shareholders versus reinvested?
data_warnings: Adjust interpretation for stock splits, bonus issues, buybacks, and other corporate actions.
Do not infer shareholder dilution from share-count changes without checking corporate actions.

rules: Every factual observation must be traceable to data or a source.
Do not claim causation from financial movements alone; describe possible explanations as hypotheses to investigate.
If data is insufficient, say so instead of fabricating an insight.

implementation_phases.name: Shareholder section and quality assurance
deliverables: Shareholder returns and capital allocation section

testing_checklist: Five observations versus four CAGR intervals test
No fabricated values or unsupported causal claims test
